name: Talia Ren
background: A Togruta survivor of Order 66 who was a Jedi youngling when the Temple fell. Smuggled offworld by a sympathetic clone trooper, she spent fifteen years hiding her connection to the Force in the Outer Rim. Working as a healer and mediator in frontier settlements, she has kept her lightsaber hidden and her gifts suppressed — until the Force began calling her back through visions she can no longer ignore.

weapons.name: Concealed lightsaber (blue crystal)
weapons.narrative_note: Built during her years at the Temple, the crystal sings faintly when danger is near. She has kept it hidden in a hollowed-out medkit for fifteen years.

armor.name: Reinforced healer's robes
armor.narrative_note: Layered linen and composite weave. Looks like simple frontier clothing but absorbs more punishment than it should.

tools.name: Frontier medical kit
tools.mechanical_effect: Enables Medicine checks. Removes 1 setback from healing attempts.
tools.narrative_note: Well-used, impeccably organized. Every settlement she has passed through has added something to it.

tools.name: Three stimpacks
tools.mechanical_effect: Can heal 5 wounds per stimpack. Three uses before resupply needed.
tools.narrative_note: Standard medical supply. She always carries more than she needs — old habit from frontier work.

special_items.name: Fragment of a Jedi holocron
special_items.mechanical_effect: Once per session, can meditate to add 1 boost die to a Lore or Discipline check related to Jedi knowledge.
special_items.narrative_note: A shard of crystal that once held the teachings of a Jedi archivist. It does not project anymore, but when she holds it, fragments of lessons surface in her mind like echoes.

special_items.name: Clone trooper dog tag
special_items.mechanical_effect: No mechanical effect. Narrative significance only.
special_items.narrative_note: CT-7729. The trooper who carried her out of the Temple. She does not know if he survived. The tag is the only proof he existed.

throughline_question: Can someone who survived by hiding ever find the courage to stand in the open again?
voice_notes: Quiet, measured. Speaks with the precision of someone who learned early that words have weight. Listens more than she talks. When she does speak, it matters. Carries grief without drowning in it. Finds beauty in small things — a sunrise, a child laughing, the hum of a healthy engine. The Force is not abstract to her; it is as real as gravity, and sometimes just as heavy.
